idea: South London veteran, mid-forties: hoarse, Estuary, twenty years on the road. Closest to the classic British TV ambulance drama, and the clearest class contrast with a posh minister.
script:
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!

Fifty over twen—
tone: A working-class woman in her mid forties from South London, with a thick Estuary accent, dropped t's and a hoarse, smoky voice. She is an NHS paramedic in the back of a speeding ambulance at night, shouting hard over the siren, raw and frightened under the authority. In the second line, nine seconds later, she is suddenly quiet and close, almost a whisper to the dying old man, and the word is cut off. Natural, gritty British television drama.
